name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 20, 2015

 A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
 Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
 Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
 Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on April 20, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

 A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
 by 5:00 p.m. on April 17, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
 posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
 Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

 *All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator Government Code Section 54956.8. The
  unimproved real property commonly referred to as “Site C” (City Housing Element)
  located on City-owned land directly adjacent to and southeasterly of the City’s
  Animal Service Center off Center Drive, and easterly of Saddleback College (Assessor
  Parcel No. 740-112-03). Agency Negotiators Dennis Wilberg, City Manager, Keith
  Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, Cheryl Dyas, Director of
  Administrative Services, Elaine Lister, Director of Community Development, and

City Council Minutes  1  April 20, 2015
   William Curley, III, City Attorney. Negotiating Party: Mission Viejo Housing
  Authority under discussion price and terms.

 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

 At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Schlicht recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
 Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council considered a real estate matter in
 closed session. The Council gave direction to proceed with a draft purchase and sale agreement
 which will go through several levels of review before coming back to the City Council for action
 in a public session.

INVOCATION: Mayor Schlicht

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim April 25, 2015, to be "Earth Day and Arbor Day"

  Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill, Program Engineer Deborah Carson and
  Environmental Programs Administrator Denise Matson discussed the Earth Day/Arbor
  Day event to be held on Saturday, April 25, 2015, from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. on Mustang
  Run at Los Alisos Boulevard. Mayor Schlicht presented Mr. Hill with the Earth Day and
  Arbor Day proclamation.

P2.  Arts Alive Presentation

  Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen and Community Services
  Supervisor Dru Mauer presented details on the upcoming Arts Alive festival to be held on
  May 2 and 3, 2015, on the Village Green outside the Norman P. Murray Community
  Center.

P3.  Presentation on the Wounded Warrior Amputee Softball Team (WWAST) Kids
  Camp

  Victor Gonzalez with the Red, White & Blue Warriors shared information on the Wounded
  Warrior Amputee Softball Kids Camp which will be held the week of June 8, 2015, at the
  Youth Athletic Fields.
City Council Minutes  2  April 20, 2015
  PUBLIC COMMENTS

 Veronica Stephens, Ladera Ranch: presented information on her non-profit organization, Action
 Force Network, which is dedicated to the prevention of sex trafficking in Orange County.

 Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: recommended that the City competitively bid the contracts that have
 been in place for 5 years or more.

 Larry Gilbert, M.V.: presented a copy of the April issue of the Community Common Sense
 newspaper and he drew the Council's attention to articles on the SDG&E substation expansion
 and the Nadadores aquatics complex. He also mentioned a recent Orange County Register
 article which referenced the renovations of the Marguerite aquatics complex pool.

 Dawn Fusco, San Juan Capistrano: spoke in opposition to SDG&E's South Orange County
 Reliability Enhancement project.

 Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: expressed concern that the traffic light at Marguerite Parkway and La Paz
 Road was out of operation last week for several hours. He noted that traffic was backed up two
 miles or more and there was no one at the intersection to direct traffic.

 Nancy French, San Juan Capistrano: detailed her opposition to SDG&E's South Orange County
 Reliability Enhancement project.

 Brian Earley, Aliso Viejo: expressed support for the Nadadores complex pool renovation.

 Roger Young, Coto de Caza: discussed the Nadadores fundraising efforts to help assist with the
 improvements of the Marguerite Aquatics Center complex.

 Jim Montrella, M.V.: presented the City Council Members with several documents including
 verification that the width and number of lanes in the 50-meter pool do meet the national and
 international swim meet standards; an article on the positive financial impacts in communities
 that run multi-day sporting events; information on the Nadadores partnership programs with
 Saddleback College and the YMCA; and a book on the Nadadores 8 year-old and under program.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Items 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, and 12 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

 Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve
 the Consent Calendar as described below.

 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  3  April 20, 2015
 AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the minutes for the regular meeting of April 6, 2015, as presented.

6.  Claim Against the City - Jennifer Holst

  Rejected claim.

7.  Pavion Park - (CIP 303) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  Faithful Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively,
  after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens
  being filed with the City and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of
  $91,324.10, thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

9.  Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 Freeway to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to negotiate and approve Contract Change Order No. 1
  with C.S. Legacy Construction, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $270,000, and; (2) adopted
  Resolution 15-15 Amending the Fiscal Year 2014-2015 Budget for Costs Related to Oso
  Parkway Widening—I-5 freeway to Country Club Drive (CIP 791).

11.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2015

  Received and filed.

13.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2015
City Council Minutes  4  April 20, 2015
   Received and filed.

14.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for February 2015

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated March 27, 2015 in the Amount of $363,530.07

  Mayor Schlicht asked if the payment made to Tomark Sports was part of the rotation plan
  for maintaining the parks and playground equipment.

  Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill responded that the expense was for
  replacement of soccer goals.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated April 3, 2015 in the Amount of $1,567,399.39

  Mayor Schlicht asked about a payment made to Hertz Equipment Rental for lights at the
  Little League fields and if the City would be better served to purchase the lights.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Rattay responded that the City rents
  additional lights for some of the fields that need extended play time but only for a few
  weeks before the annual time change.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  April 20, 2015
 5.  First Amendment to Professional Services Agreement for Affordable Housing
  Consulting and Technical Services

  Council Member Sachs announced that he had some questions on this item but he needed
  further time to locate his notes (a vote to defer the matter was taken with item 12 below.)

8.  Sierra Recreation Center Play Area - (CIP 323) - Notice of Completion

  Council Member Sachs asked about consulting fees for not only this project, but for all
  projects in general. He told City Manager Wilberg that he'd like to see if staff can come
  up with a formula that limits the consulting fees to a percentage of the project so consulting
  costs don't become a heavy burden on the overall price of a project.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) certify
  the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the
  City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record
  Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful Performance
  and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City and (4) authorize the payment of the final retention of $25,437.80, thirty-five
  (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10.  2015 Residential Resurfacing-CDBG Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP
  838)

  Council Member Sachs asked if the dollars were carried over from the previous year at a
  proportional rate.

  Director of Public Works Chagnon responded that the funds remaining in the budget from
  last year are roughly equal to the cost of the streets which were deferred for this year's
  project.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to approve
  the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer, and
  authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  6  April 20, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

12.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2015

  Council Member Sachs announced that he is having trouble locating his notes for this item
  and item number 5.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to table items
  5 and 12 to the next City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

*Items 22 and 24 were considered together.

Council Member Ury

22.  Mayor’s letter to CPUC Regarding San Juan Capistrano Substation

  Council Member Ury presented his agenda report.

Mayor Schlicht

24.  Report to the Public on City Council positions relating to the SDG&E South Orange
  County Reliability Enhancement Project

  Mayor Schlicht presented her report and provided a response to Council Member Ury's
  report.

  The following expressed opposition to Council Member Ury’s recommended action: Joe
  Tully, M.V.; Julie Tully, M.V.; Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.; and Rhen Kohan, San Juan
  Capistrano.

City Council Minutes  7  April 20, 2015
   The following noted support for Council Member Ury’s recommendation: Rhonda
  Reardon, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to write
  a letter to the CPUC to advise that the Council has taken a position on this matter and
  clarifying that the Mayor's letter is not the official position of the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum and Ury
  NOES:  Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht,
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:26 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:41
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Community Services Commission Vacancy

  By consensus, the City Council accepted the letter of resignation from Commissioner Brian
  Porter.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  appoint Brian Goodell to serve on the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report/Discussion of AB1217

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

  The City Council discussed the potential repercussions of AB1217 and the diminished
  representation that south county cities would have if the OCFA Board was reduced in size.

City Council Minutes  8  April 20, 2015
   By consensus, the City Council directed staff to draft a follow-up letter to OCFA with some
  ideas for the makeup of the OCFA Board and return to the City Council in two weeks for
  approval of the letter.

17.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.

18.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

19.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: speaking to item 16, he discussed problems at the Orange County
Fire Authority and he thanked the reform-minded individuals who are now on the Board of
Directors and have made some changes. Mr. Wontrobski recommended that the City Council
strongly oppose AB1217 in their letter to the OCFA Board.

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney Bill Curley informed the City Council that the San Juan Capistrano tiered water
case decision came out earlier in the day. The court ruled that tiered rates in and of themselves
are not unconstitutional however, San Juan Capistrano did not follow proper calculation methods
and therefore, their tiered rates were ruled unconstitutional. Mr. Curley agreed to provide a copy
of the ruling to the Council Members for their information.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

 Council Member Bucknum

 Council Member Bucknum announced that she is looking forward to the Earth Day event on
 Saturday at Mustang Run. The street will be closed so it will be easy for residents and
 community groups to participate in the volunteer planting. She noted that she is also looking
City Council Minutes  9  April 20, 2015
  forward to the upcoming Arts Alive Festival with its new Food and Wine Festival
 component. Council Member Bucknum reminded residents that the Mission Viejo Relay for
 Life is coming up June 6 and 7, 2015, and now is the time to form a team. She recommended
 that individuals or groups register to participate in the event that benefits the American Cancer
 Society and is Orange County’s largest and most profitable Relay. Addressing residents Victor
 and Eileen Gonzalez, Council Member Bucknum congratulated their daughter and the Mission
 Viejo High School Color Guard which recently took 6th place in a national competition. She
 further announced that on Thursday, April 23, the City’s mosque will be hosting a leadership
 summit. The mosque recently issued a letter speaking out against the atrocities that are being
 made by ISIS and she commended the mosque leaders for doing so. She further encouraged
 residents and her colleagues to attend the summit where the issue of terrorism will be addressed.
 Council Member Bucknum shared the sad news that a Trabuco Hills High School student
 recently died of a prescription drug overdose. She stated that it is important that we continue to
 bring awareness to the issue and in that vein, there will be a public screening of Part 1 of An
 Invisible Line, which is the four-part Mission Viejo Television series on the subject of teen drug
 abuse in the community. The screening will take place on April 30 from 7:00 to 8:30 p.m. at
 the Murray Community Center. Council Member Bucknum commended Orange County
 Register reporters David Whiting and Tomoya Shimura for two good articles on the history and
 heritage of Mission Viejo. She encouraged residents to rely on these good journalists' reporting
 and to not rely on blog newspapers.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs notified staff that the large “open for business” banners were posted at the
apartments on Oso Parkway over the weekend. He stated that he thought they had been removed
and he asked that they be taken down again.

21.  Research the Designation of Political Free Speech Zones in Specific Areas of the City’s
  right-of-way, where Campaign Signs Could be Legally Placed for 30 days Prior to
  any Local or Regional Election

  Council Member Sachs presented his report.
  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) direct
  staff to research designating political free speech zones in specific areas of the City's right-
  of-way, where campaign signs could be legally placed for 30 days prior to any local or
  regional election; and (2) prepare the necessary revision to the City's sign regulations for a
  noticed public hearing, review and recommendation by the Planning and Transportation
  Commission to the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  10  April 20, 2015
 Council Member Ury

23.  Response to State Mandated Water Conservation Regulations

  Council Member Ury presented his report.

  Jonathan Volzke, Public Information Manager, Santa Margarita Water District: expressed
  the Santa Margarita Water District's support and thanks for the City's drought conservation
  efforts.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to appropriate
  $50,000 from reserves for the immediate response by City staff to implement state-
  mandated drought regulations over the next two months.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Schlicht announced that she voted no because she thought staff would need to bring
  back areas of concern and that it was putting the cart before the horse.

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he will continue to champion the drought issue. He noted
 that residents have reduced their usage by 2-3% but it needs to go a bit further than that. Santa
 Margarita Water District has invited students to participate in a water awareness poster and
 slogan program as well as water awareness photography and digital art contests. He outlined
 the prizes and he encouraged students to get involved and enter. Mayor Pro Tem Raths reiterated
 Council Member Bucknum’s invitation to the screening of An Invisible Line to learn about the
 prescription drug abuse problems in and around Mission Viejo. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Raths
 announced that the Mission Viejo Rotary Club is holding a charity poker tournament on
 Saturday, June 13, 2015, and residents can register at mvtexasholdem.com.

 Mayor Schlicht

 Discussing the drought issue, Mayor Schlicht suggested that there be a contest in the community
 to gather suggestions on how to save water. She noted that she and her family used to run the
 washing machine hose out to the front yard to recycle the water and put it to good use. She also
 reminded the community that Arts Alive will take place on May 2 and 3 and she encouraged
 residents to attend. Mayor Schlicht stated that public office is a public trust and it should only
 be used to advance the public interest and protect the health, safety and welfare of the

City Council Minutes  11  April 20, 2015
  community. She said that Council Members should avoid appearances of impropriety and
 encourage public participation. Mayor Schlicht noted that her motto remains, “public disclosure
 and public consent” and she concluded with a quote from Theodore Roosevelt: "We cannot
 afford to differ on the question of honesty if we expect our republic permanently to
 endure. Honesty is not so much a credit as an absolute prerequisite to efficient service to the
 public. Unless a man is honest, we have no right to keep him in public life; it matters not how
 brilliant his capacity."

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 9:49 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, May 4, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________________
 Karen Hamman, City Clerk

 Approved at the meeting of May 4, 2015

City Council Minutes  12  April 20, 2015
